1428982245751144449.name: Emre Aslanger
1428982245751144449.text: @ED_Ultrasounder It is obvious but worth repeating: ECG does not show the culprit, it shows the area of ischemia and this can be influenced by coronary anatomy, previous MIs, collateral flow, multiple stenoses etc.

1524368898988072961.name: Stephen W. Smith
1524368898988072961.text:
Newly published article confirms what we know from anecdote: Cardiologists don't follow NonSTEMI guidelines, which state: patients with persistent chest pain, or instability, or pulm edema, should go within 2 hours to cath lab regardless of ECG or trop.

https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/clc.23781

1524716908880224256.name: Emre Aslanger
1524716908880224256.text: @smithECGBlog The other side of the coin is that these recommendations are not well evidence-based. I especially doubt poor hemodynamics and heart failure without clear evidence of ischemia. Mechanic complications are there for early surgery, which is also a kind of myth.

Review of DDx for Tall R' in V1: 'R-WAVED'

- RBBB or left-sided Vtach
- WPW - left-sided 
- Acute posterior MI
- Ventricular hypertrophy (RVH, HOCM)
- Embolism
- Dextrocardia, Displaced leads, Dystrophy
